newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed higher across the board. November added $29 to close at $1,550, while January gained $13 to close at $1,450 per tonne. Speculative and fund buying as well as industry interest at the lows helped underpin values. In New York arabica futures ended moderately lower in quiet dealings. December shed 1.50 cents to close at 120.75 cents/lb while March gave up 85 points to close at 113.10 cents/lb.

There is continued talk of some coffee moving to the board which undermined sentiment. The reason cited for the easing in supplies is because of large shipments by Brazil, but if much of this was committed already it should have little bearing on the market, not to mention that Brazilians are not deliverable, trade sources said. However, the rationale is that coffee that was substituted for the lack of Brazilians prior to this will no longer be in as great a demand. Traders said that in spite of the fall today the uptrend is still intact and may last through the end of the year. Thereafter, the supply situation is expected to ease.

HONDURAS - According to trade sources Hurricane Marcos may have caused damage to the Honduran crop. The rains have hit the lower mountain areas the worst, just as the crop there was entering into full swing. The area accounts for about 25 per cent of Honduran coffee production. So far it had been assumed, that 1996/97 (October/September) coffee production would be slightly above last year's total of 2.3 million bags.

GUATEMALA - Guatemalan coffee exports in October 1996 reached 133,951 60-kg bags which compares to 134,800 bags during October 1995, the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) said. Max Quirin, departing president of Anacafe, said that this is a signal that exports during 1996/97 are going to be very similar to 1995/96 exports.

NETHERLANDS - The Netherlands imported 229,758 bags of coffee in July 1996 nearly 15 percent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.823 million bags, nearly 12 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped slightly to 2.910 million bags down from 2.963 million bags imported in 1994. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Uganda (120,600 vs 133,000 bags), El Salvador (110,600 vs 54,900 bags) and Colombia (276,700 vs 246,900 bags). The country exported 335,800 bags of coffee in January/July 1996, 3.7 percent less than in the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 15 percent to 616,900 bags.
